extracted.intended_audience: individuals and entities (and their counsel) who may be required to register under FARA; FARA eFile users; members of the public seeking FARA records
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of who must register under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, what disclosures are required, how filings are administered and submitted (including eFile/MFA requirements), and how to obtain records or review materials at the FARA public office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who must register
rubrics_metrics.description: FARA requires certain agents of foreign principals who are engaged in political activities or other activities specified under the statute to make periodic public disclosure of their relationship with the foreign principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page states this as the core registration trigger — agents of foreign principals engaged in political or other specified activities must register so their relationships and activities are publicly disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required disclosures (content of registration statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must make periodic public disclosure of their relationship with the foreign principal, as well as activities, receipts and disbursements in support of those activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure must include the relationship with the foreign principal and financial information (receipts and disbursements) tied to the relevant activities. Registration statements are available online at fara.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periodicity of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants are required to make 'periodic' public disclosures under the statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The landing page uses the term 'periodic public disclosure' but does not specify filing intervals on this page; users should consult registration forms/templates or the statute for specific filing frequencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administration and enforcement responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The FARA Unit of the Counterintelligence and Export Control Section (CES) in the National Security Division (NSD) is responsible for the administration and enforcement of FARA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact information and the Public Office are provided for inquiries and record review; the Unit handles determinations and enforcement actions under the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to registration statements and records
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration statements are available online at fara.gov by using the available search tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials that are not available online can be reviewed in person at the FARA Unit Public Office by appointment; appointments are only necessary to review materials not currently available online.

rubrics_metrics.name: FARA public office appointment procedure and hours
rubrics_metrics.description: The FARA Unit Public Office is open on official business days by appointment only between 11 a.m. and 3 p.m. for in-person review of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To schedule an appointment, contact the FARA Unit at (202) 233-0777. Deliveries and office hours for deliveries are Monday - Friday, 8:30 a.m. - 5:00 p.m.; public office hours: Monday - Friday, 11:00 a.m. - 3:00 p.m.

rubrics_metrics.name: FARA eFile authentication requirement (DOJ Login and MFA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective February 6, 2026, the DOJ updated the FARA eFile system to utilize the DOJ Login platform for authentication of all new and existing users; all users will be required to enroll in DOJ Login and register MFA credentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory authentication change to comply with federal multi-factor authentication requirements; the page directs users to click the provided link and use the 'Sign up' link to register an account with DOJ Login.

rubrics_metrics.name: FARA eFile system status notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The FARA eFile application is currently experiencing technical issues that cause delays or the inability to successfully complete and submit a filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The technical team is working toward a solution; the notice (dated February 5, 2026) alerts users to potential delays and issues when attempting to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of required disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure of the required information facilitates evaluation by the government and the American people of the activities of such persons in light of their function as foreign agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The landing page states this as the declarative purpose of FARA disclosure requirements — transparency to permit evaluation of foreign influence and activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to get help and contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Public information relating to FARA may be obtained by contacting the Department of Justice/NSD FARA Unit (phone and email provided) or by visiting the Public Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact: (202) 233-0776; fara.public@usdoj.gov; Public Office address and hours provided. Use these channels for appointment scheduling, inquiries about registration, and record access.
